question:
What is subtracted from GDP to arrive at NDP?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Subsidies
Depreciation
Net indirect taxes
Net factor income from abroad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Depreciation

Explanation:
To calculate NDP (Net Domestic Product), Depreciation is subtracted from GDP (Gross Domestic Product). Depreciation is also known as 'Capital Consumption Allowance'. It represents the wear and tear of capital goods (like machinery, buildings, etc.) used in the production process. GDP includes depreciation, whereas NDP excludes it. Thus, NDP better reflects the real economic production capacity of a country.

Extra Facts:
GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period. NDP is derived by subtracting depreciation from GDP, indicating the net production capacity of the country. Apart from depreciation, GNP (Gross National Product) is calculated by adding Net Factor Income from Abroad to GDP.

☛ What is the difference between GDP and NDP? → Depreciation
☛ How is GNP calculated? → GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad
☛ What is National Income? → NNP at Factor Cost
☛ What is the full form of NDP? → Net Domestic Product
☛ What is depreciation also called? → Capital Consumption Allowance
question_hi:
एनडीपी (NDP) निकालने के लिए जीडीपी (GDP) में से क्या घटाया जाता है?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options_hi: अनुदान
मूल्यह्रास
शुद्ध अप्रत्यक्ष कर
विदेश से शुद्ध कारक आय
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation)

Explanation:
NDP (Net Domestic Product) की गणना करने के लिए GDP (Gross Domestic Product) में से मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) को घटाया जाता है। मूल्यह्रास को 'पूंजी की खपत' (Capital Consumption Allowance) भी कहा जाता है। यह उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग होने वाली पूंजीगत वस्तुओं (जैसे मशीनरी, भवन आदि) के मूल्य में ह्रास को दर्शाता है। GDP में मूल्यह्रास शामिल होता है, जबकि NDP में इसे घटा दिया जाता है। इस प्रकार, NDP देश की वास्तविक आर्थिक उत्पादन क्षमता को बेहतर ढंग से प्रदर्शित करता है।

Extra Facts:
GDP एक देश की सीमा के भीतर एक निश्चित समयावधि में उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के बाजार मूल्य का योग है। NDP GDP में से मूल्यह्रास घटाकर प्राप्त किया जाता है, जो देश की शुद्ध उत्पादन क्षमता को दर्शाता है। मूल्यह्रास के अलावा, GNP (Gross National Product) प्राप्त करने के लिए GDP में विदेश से शुद्ध कारक आय (Net Factor Income from Abroad) जोड़ी जाती है।

☛ मूल्यह्रास को क्या कहा जाता है? → पूंजी की खपत

question:
Which formula is used for the calculation of Ex Ante Aggregate Demand?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: C+I-cY
C+cY
cY-C+I
C+I+cY
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is C+I+cY

Explanation:
Ex Ante Aggregate Demand refers to the total planned expenditure in an economy, consisting of consumption (C), investment (I), and government spending (G), which depends on income (Y). The formula for its calculation is:
AD=C+I+cY
Here,
- C = Autonomous consumption (independent of income)
- I = Autonomous investment
- cY = Income-dependent consumption (where c is the marginal propensity to consume)
This formula is central to Keynesian economics for short-term macroeconomic analysis.

Extra Facts:
- The equilibrium between Aggregate Demand (AD) and Aggregate Supply (AS) determines the Equilibrium Income.
- Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is the ratio of change in consumption to change in income.
- The Multiplier Effect explains how changes in aggregate demand impact national income.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is Aggregate Demand? → Total demand in an economy
☛ What is the formula for MPC? → ΔCΔY
☛ Which economist is associated with the Multiplier Effect? → Keynes
☛ When does equilibrium income occur? → When AD = AS
☛ What is autonomous consumption? → Consumption independent of income
question_hi:
प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग (Ex Ante Aggregate Demand) की गणना के लिए किस सूत्र का उपयोग किया जाता है ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: C+I-cY
C+cY
cY-C+I
C+I+cY
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है C+I+cY

Explanation:
प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग (Ex Ante Aggregate Demand) का अर्थ है अर्थव्यवस्था में उपभोग (C), निवेश (I) और सरकारी व्यय (G) का योग, जो आय (Y) पर निर्भर करता है। इसकी गणना के लिए सूत्र है:
AD=C+I+cY
यहाँ,
- C = स्वायत्त उपभोग (आय से स्वतंत्र)
- I = स्वायत्त निवेश
- cY = आय पर निर्भर उपभोग (जहाँ c सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति है)
यह सूत्र कीनेसियन अर्थशास्त्र में समग्र मांग को दर्शाता है, जो अल्पकालिक आर्थिक विश्लेषण के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

Extra Facts:
- समग्र मांग (AD) और समग्र पूर्ति (AS) का संतुलन ही साम्य आय (Equilibrium Income) निर्धारित करता है।
- सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) वह अनुपात है जो बताता है कि आय में वृद्धि का कितना भाग उपभोग पर खर्च किया जाता है।
- गुणक प्रभाव (Multiplier Effect) की अवधारणा समग्र मांग में परिवर्तन के प्रभाव को दर्शाती है।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (MPC) का सूत्र क्या है? → ΔCΔY
☛ गुणक प्रभाव किस अर्थशास्त्री से संबंधित है? → कीन्स
☛ साम्य आय कब होती है? → जब AD = AS
☛ स्वायत्त उपभोग क्या है? → आय से स्वतंत्र उपभोग

question:
What correctly defines change of inventories of a firm during a year ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the previous year – Sale of the firm during the year
Sale of the firm during the year – Production of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the previous year
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year

Explanation:
The change in inventories is defined as the difference between a firm's production and sales during a year. If production exceeds sales, inventories increase, and if sales exceed production, inventories decrease. This concept is crucial in 'National Income Accounting' as it represents changes in a firm's 'stock'. It is also called 'Inventory Investment', which is a part of 'Investment'.

Extra Facts:
☛ Change in inventories is also termed as 'change in stock' and helps balance 'savings' and 'investment'.
☛ If Production > Sales → Inventories rise (positive change).
☛ If Sales > Production → Inventories fall (negative change).
☛ Change in inventories is included in GDP (Gross Domestic Product) calculation as it is a component of 'Investment'.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is change in inventories called? → Production – Sales
☛ What is inventory change termed in GDP? → Inventory Investment
☛ If Sales > Production, what happens to inventories? → Decreases
☛ Why is inventory change important in national income accounting? → Part of Investment
☛ What does change in stock indicate? → Difference in inventories
question_hi:
एक वर्ष के दौरान फर्म की माल-सूची में परिवर्तन को निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प सही ढंग से परिभाषित करता है ?

वर्ष के दौरान फर्म की बिक्री – वर्ष के दौरान फर्म का उत्पादन

☛ माल-सूची में परिवर्तन को GDP (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) की गणना में शामिल किया जाता है क्योंकि यह 'निवेश' का एक हिस्सा है।

question:
Which of the following represents disposable income?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions

Explanation:
Disposable Income refers to the income available to individuals and households after deducting taxes and other mandatory deductions (such as social security contributions). This income is available for consumption and savings. It is also known as Personal Disposable Income. It is a crucial concept in economic analysis as it influences consumption behavior and savings rates. Disposable Income is derived by subtracting taxes and other deductions from Gross Income.

Extra Facts:
Disposable Income is primarily used for consumption and savings. It is a key component of National Income. According to Keynesian Theory, disposable income is the main determinant of the consumption function, represented as C = a + bYd (where Yd is disposable income). Disposable Income is a vital indicator for understanding Aggregate Demand in an economy.

☛ What does the consumption function represent? → C = a + bYd
☛ What is the difference between gross income and disposable income? → Taxes and deductions
☛ What is Keynes' main theory? → Effective Demand
☛ What is the balance of savings and investment called? → Savings-Investment Equality

निम्नलिखित में से क्या प्रयोज्य आय (disposable income) को दर्शाता है?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options_hi: करों और अन्य कटौतियों के बाद व्यक्तियों और परिवारों द्वारा अर्जित आय

व्यक्तियों द्वारा अपने स्वयं के व्यवसाय या स्वरोजगार के माध्यम से अर्जित आय
करों और अन्य कटौतियों से पहले व्यक्तियों और परिवारों द्वारा अर्जित कुल आय
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है करों और अन्य कटौतियों के बाद व्यक्तियों और परिवारों द्वारा अर्जित आय

Explanation:
प्रयोज्य आय (Disposable Income) वह आय है जो व्यक्तियों और परिवारों को करों और अन्य अनिवार्य कटौतियों (जैसे सामाजिक सुरक्षा योगदान) के बाद प्राप्त होती है। यह आय उपभोग और बचत के लिए उपलब्ध होती है। इसे व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय (Personal Disposable Income) भी कहा जाता है। यह आर्थिक विश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह उपभोग व्यवहार और बचत दर को प्रभावित करती है। कुल आय (Gross Income) से करों और अन्य कटौतियों को घटाकर प्रयोज्य आय प्राप्त की जाती है।

Extra Facts:
प्रयोज्य आय का उपयोग मुख्य रूप से उपभोग (Consumption) और बचत (Savings) के लिए किया जाता है। यह राष्ट्रीय आय (National Income) का एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है। केन्ज़ के सिद्धांत (Keynesian Theory) के अनुसार, प्रयोज्य आय उपभोग फलन (Consumption Function) का मुख्य निर्धारक है, जिसे C = a + bYd (जहाँ Yd प्रयोज्य आय है) से दर्शाया जाता है। अर्थव्यवस्था में मांग (Aggregate Demand) को समझने के लिए प्रयोज्य आय एक महत्वपूर्ण संकेतक है।

question:
Which of the following is true about disposable income in relation to personal income?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Disposable income is equal to personal income.
Disposable income is always less than personal income.
Disposable income is always greater than personal income.
Disposable income can be greater or less than personal income, depending on taxes and deductions.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Disposable income is always less than personal income.

Explanation:
Disposable income is the amount of money available to an individual after deducting taxes and other mandatory deductions (like social security contributions) from personal income. Since taxes and deductions are always applicable, disposable income will always be less than personal income. This concept is crucial in economics for understanding income distribution and consumption behavior.

Extra Facts:
- Disposable Income = Personal Income - Personal Taxes - Mandatory Deductions.
- It is the income available for consumption and savings.
- In Keynesian Economics, disposable income is a key determinant of the consumption function, which influences aggregate demand.
- If government subsidies or transfer payments increase, disposable income may rise, but it still remains less than personal income.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is personal income? → Total income earned by individuals
☛ How is disposable income calculated? → Personal Income - Taxes - Deductions
☛ Which income is used for consumption and savings? → Disposable Income
☛ What is not included in national income? → Transfer Payments
☛ What is the main determinant of the consumption function? → Disposable Income

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है प्रयोज्य आय हमेशा वैयक्तिक आय से कम होती है।

Explanation:
प्रयोज्य आय (Disposable Income) वह आय है जो व्यक्ति के पास करों और अन्य अनिवार्य कटौतियों (जैसे सामाजिक सुरक्षा योगदान) के बाद बचती है। वैयक्तिक आय (Personal Income) में से व्यक्तिगत कर (Income Tax) और अन्य कटौतियाँ घटाने के बाद ही प्रयोज्य आय प्राप्त होती है। चूँकि कर और कटौतियाँ हमेशा लागू होती हैं, इसलिए प्रयोज्य आय हमेशा वैयक्तिक आय से कम होगी। यह अर्थशास्त्र में आय वितरण और उपभोग व्यवहार को समझने के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण अवधारणा है।

- केनेसियन अर्थशास्त्र (Keynesian Economics) में, प्रयोज्य आय उपभोग फलन (Consumption Function) का मुख्य निर्धारक है, जो कुल मांग (Aggregate Demand) को प्रभावित करता है।

question:
Select the correct statement.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Slope of the consumption function is indicated by APC, and not MPC.
MPC multiplied by MPS equals 1.
Investment multiplier is positively related to MPC.
Investment multiplier is zero when MPS is zero.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "Investment multiplier is positively related to MPC."

Explanation:
The concept of the Investment Multiplier was introduced by John Maynard Keynes. It shows how much total income increases due to an initial increase in investment. The formula for the multiplier (K) is: K = 1 / (1 - MPC) or K = 1 / MPS, where MPC is the Marginal Propensity to Consume and MPS is the Marginal Propensity to Save. Since MPC + MPS = 1, an increase in MPC leads to a decrease in MPS, thereby increasing the multiplier. Thus, the investment multiplier has a positive relationship with MPC.

Extra Facts:
1. Difference between APC (Average Propensity to Consume) and MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume): APC is the ratio of total consumption to total income, while MPC is the ratio of change in consumption to change in income.
2. According to Keynes, MPC + MPS = 1, as income is either consumed or saved.
3. If MPS is zero, the investment multiplier becomes infinite (K = 1/0), not zero, because all additional income is spent on consumption.

सही कथन का चयन कीजिए ।

[RRC GROUP D]
options_hi: उपभोग फलन की प्रवणता APC द्वारा इंगित की जाती है, न कि MPC द्वारा।
MPC को MPS से गुणा करने पर 1 के बराबर मान प्राप्त होता है।
निवेश गुणक, MPC के साथ धनात्मक रूप से संबंधित होता है।
MPS शून्य होने पर निवेश गुणक शून्य होता है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है "निवेश गुणक, MPC के साथ धनात्मक रूप से संबंधित होता है।"

Explanation:
निवेश गुणक (Investment Multiplier) की अवधारणा जॉन मेनार्ड कीन्स द्वारा प्रतिपादित की गई थी। यह दर्शाता है कि निवेश में प्रारंभिक वृद्धि से आय में कितनी गुना वृद्धि होगी। निवेश गुणक (K) का सूत्र है: K = 1 / (1 - MPC) या K = 1 / MPS, जहाँ MPC सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति (Marginal Propensity to Consume) और MPS सीमांत बचत प्रवृत्ति (Marginal Propensity to Save) है। चूँकि MPC और MPS का योग 1 होता है, इसलिए यदि MPC बढ़ता है तो MPS घटता है और निवेश गुणक बढ़ता है। इस प्रकार, निवेश गुणक MPC के साथ धनात्मक संबंध रखता है।

Extra Facts:
1. APC (औसत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति) और MPC (सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति) में अंतर: APC कुल उपभोग को कुल आय से विभाजित करके प्राप्त होता है, जबकि MPC आय में परिवर्तन से उपभोग में परिवर्तन का अनुपात है।
2. कीन्स के अनुसार, MPC + MPS = 1, क्योंकि आय या तो उपभोग की जाती है या बचत की जाती है।
3. यदि MPS शून्य हो, तो निवेश गुणक अनंत होगा (K = 1/0), न कि शून्य, क्योंकि सारी अतिरिक्त आय उपभोग में खर्च होगी।

question:
What is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the context of National Income Accounting?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: The total exports of a country
The total savings of a nation
The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period
The total income of a country's government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period

Explanation:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is a key indicator of a country's economic activity. It represents the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders during a specific period (usually a year). GDP can be calculated using three methods: Production Approach, Income Approach, and Expenditure Approach. It is a crucial tool for measuring economic growth and development. Only final products are included in GDP to avoid double-counting of intermediate goods.

Extra Facts:
The three main components of GDP are: Consumption (C), Investment (I), Government Spending (G), and Net Exports (NX). GDP can be divided into Nominal GDP and Real GDP, where Real GDP adjusts for inflation. Besides GDP, Gross National Product (GNP) is another important indicator, measuring the value produced by a country's citizens both domestically and abroad.

☛ Which type of products are included in GDP? → Only final products
☛ Who calculates GDP in India? → Central Statistics Office (CSO)

Explanation:
सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) एक देश की आर्थिक गतिविधि का एक प्रमुख संकेतक है। यह किसी विशिष्ट अवधि (आमतौर पर एक वर्ष) में एक देश की सीमाओं के भीतर उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का बाजार मूल्य है। GDP की गणना तीन प्रकार से की जा सकती है: उत्पादन विधि, आय विधि और व्यय विधि। यह देश की आर्थिक वृद्धि और विकास को मापने का एक महत्वपूर्ण उपकरण है। GDP में केवल अंतिम उत्पादों को शामिल किया जाता है, मध्यवर्ती उत्पादों को नहीं, ताकि दोहरी गणना से बचा जा सके।

Extra Facts:
GDP के तीन प्रमुख घटक हैं: उपभोग (C), निवेश (I), सरकारी व्यय (G), और शुद्ध निर्यात (NX)। GDP को नाममात्र GDP और वास्तविक GDP में विभाजित किया जा सकता है, जहां वास्तविक GDP मुद्रास्फीति के प्रभाव को समायोजित करता है। GDP के अलावा, सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) भी एक महत्वपूर्ण संकेतक है, जो देश के नागरिकों द्वारा देश के अंदर और बाहर उत्पादित मूल्य को मापता है।

question:
While calculating Net National Product (NNP), what is subtracted from Gross National Product (GNP)?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Subsidies
Depreciation
Personal income
Indirect taxes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Depreciation

Explanation:
While calculating Net National Product (NNP), Depreciation is subtracted from Gross National Product (GNP). Depreciation, also called 'Capital Consumption Allowance', represents the wear and tear of capital assets (e.g., machinery, buildings) used in the production process. It is a non-cash expense reflecting the reduction in asset value over time. NNP is the 'net' measure of GNP as it adjusts for the consumption of capital during production. Thus, NNP = GNP – Depreciation.

Extra Facts:
• GNP measures the market value of all final goods/services produced by a country's citizens in a year, whether domestically or abroad.
• NNP reflects the economy’s true production capacity by accounting for capital depreciation.
• Depreciation rates are typically determined by government/global standards.

☛ Key difference between GDP and GNP? → Net Income from Abroad

The value of GDP at the current prevailing prices is called_________.

solution:

Explanation:
Nominal GDP is the GDP measured at current market prices, reflecting inflation or deflation effects. Unlike real GDP (adjusted for price changes using a base year), it does not accurately represent actual economic growth. Nominal GDP is often used for short-term economic analysis, while real GDP is a better indicator of long-term growth as it eliminates price fluctuations. The distinction is critical for policy-making and inflation impact assessment.

Extra Facts:
GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country’s borders in a specific period. It is calculated via three methods: production, income, and expenditure approaches. question:
_______ is calculated by dividing the nominal GDP in a given year by the real GDP for the same year and multiplying it by 100.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Disposable Income
GDP Deflator
Real Income
Per Capita Income
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GDP Deflator

Explanation:
The GDP Deflator is a key economic indicator used to measure the price level in an economy. It represents the ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP, calculated as GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100. Unlike other options such as Disposable Income, Real Income, or Per Capita Income, the GDP Deflator specifically measures inflation or deflation by comparing the current prices (Nominal GDP) to base-year prices (Real GDP). It is a broad measure as it includes all goods and services produced domestically, making it distinct from the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Extra Facts:
The GDP Deflator and CPI both measure inflation but differ in scope. The GDP Deflator covers all goods and services produced in the economy, while CPI only includes consumer goods and services. Additionally, the GDP Deflator excludes imported goods, whereas CPI includes them. The GDP Deflator is also preferred for analyzing long-term inflation trends as it is not affected by changes in consumption patterns.

solution_hi:

question:
The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as ________.

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: gross national product
net national product
gross domestic product
net domestic product
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gross Domestic Product

Explanation:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in one year. It is a primary indicator used to measure the size and health of an economy. GDP includes only final products, not intermediate goods, to avoid double counting. It can be measured from three approaches - production, income and expenditure. GDP does not include income earned from abroad, which distinguishes it from Gross National Product (GNP).

Extra Facts:
GDP is measured based on contributions from three major sectors - agriculture, industry and services. In India, GDP is calculated by the Central Statistics Office (CSO). There are two main types of GDP - Nominal GDP (at current prices) and Real GDP (at constant prices, removing inflation effects). GDP growth rate is a crucial indicator of economic performance.

Explanation:
सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) एक वर्ष के दौरान किसी देश की सीमाओं के भीतर उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मौद्रिक मूल्य है। यह अर्थव्यवस्था के आकार और स्वास्थ्य को मापने का एक प्रमुख संकेतक है। GDP में केवल अंतिम उत्पादों को शामिल किया जाता है, मध्यवर्ती उत्पादों को नहीं, ताकि दोहरी गणना से बचा जा सके। यह उत्पादन, आय और व्यय तीनों दृष्टिकोणों से मापा जा सकता है। GDP की गणना में विदेशों से प्राप्त आय को शामिल नहीं किया जाता है, जो इसे सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) से अलग करता है।

question:
The _________is a macroeconomic term that refers to the proportion of income that is saved rather than spent on current goods and services.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Marginal propensity to save
Average propensity to save
Marginal propensity to consume
Average propensity to consume
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Average propensity to save

Explanation:
Average Propensity to Save (APS) is a macroeconomic concept that represents the ratio of total savings to total income. It is expressed by the formula APS = Savings/Income. It indicates what portion of income is saved rather than spent on consumption. This is a key part of Keynes' income theory and helps in understanding the balance between savings and investment in an economy.

Extra Facts:
Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) shows the change in savings due to a change in income, while APS reflects the relationship between total income and total savings. According to Keynes, APS increases with rising income as people tend to save more. This concept plays a crucial role in national income determination and the savings-investment model.

☛ According to Keynes, how does APS change with rising income? → Increases
☛ In which model is the balance between savings and investment analyzed? → Keynesian Model

question:
Which of the following is NOT true about the circular flow of income in a two-sector economy?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Total production is equal to total consumption.
Factor payment is equal to factor income.
Real Flow is more than money flow.
Consumption expenditure is equal to factor income.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Real Flow is more than money flow.

Explanation:
In a two-sector economy, the circular flow of income occurs between households and firms. In this model, total production is equal to total consumption because households consume all goods and services produced by firms. Factor payment is equal to factor income as firms pay households for the resources (like labor, capital) they provide. Consumption expenditure is equal to factor income because households spend all their income on consumption. However, real flow and money flow are equal to each other, not one being more than the other. This is why this option is incorrect.

Extra Facts:
In a two-sector economy, there is no government or foreign sector involved, making the model simple. Real flow involves the flow of goods and services, while money flow involves the flow of money. These two flows are always equal in quantity because every good or service has a monetary value. This model does not include savings and investments, making it even simpler.

द्वि क्षेत्रीय अर्थव्यवस्था में आय का चक्रीय प्रवाह घरों और फर्मों के बीच होता है। इस मॉडल में, कुल उत्पादन, कुल खपत के बराबर होता है क्योंकि घर फर्मों द्वारा उत्पादित सभी वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का उपभोग करते हैं। कारक भुगतान, कारक आय के बराबर होता है क्योंकि फर्में घरों को उनके द्वारा प्रदान किए गए संसाधनों (जैसे श्रम, पूंजी) के लिए भुगतान करती हैं। खपत व्यय, कारक आय के बराबर होता है क्योंकि घर अपनी सारी आय खपत पर खर्च करते हैं। हालांकि, वास्तविक प्रवाह और मुद्रा प्रवाह एक-दूसरे के बराबर होते हैं, न कि एक दूसरे से अधिक। यही कारण है कि यह विकल्प सही नहीं है।

question:
Which of the following options does NOT constitute a national income measurement method?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Credit method.
Product method
Income method
Expenditure method
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Credit method

Explanation:
The three main methods for measuring national income are: Product method, Income method, and Expenditure method. These methods are used to calculate the total economic activity of a country. The Product method sums up the market value of all final goods and services produced. The Income method aggregates all factor incomes (wages, profits, rent, interest). The Expenditure method totals all expenditures on final uses (consumption, investment, government spending, net exports). The Credit method is not a recognized approach for national income measurement, making it the correct answer.

Extra Facts:
National income is measured using indicators like GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and GNP (Gross National Product). GDP represents the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year, while GNP includes income earned by citizens abroad. The Value Added Method is a variant of the Product method, where value addition at each production stage is summed.

Extra Facts:

question:
What does GNP stand for ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Gramin Nisak Praman
Gramin Nigam Parishad
Gross National Product
Gross National Produce
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gross National Product

Explanation:
GNP stands for Gross National Product. It represents the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's citizens in a given time period (usually one year), whether the production takes place within the country or abroad. GNP includes GDP (Gross Domestic Product) plus net income from abroad. It is a crucial economic indicator that helps measure a nation's economic health and standard of living.

Extra Facts:
Key points about GNP calculation:
1. It includes only final goods and services, not intermediate goods.
2. GNP excludes transfer payments like pensions and unemployment benefits.
3. GNP can be measured at factor cost or market prices.
4. GNP includes depreciation, while NNP (Net National Product) deducts depreciation.
5. The formula is: GNP = GDP + Net Income from Abroad

Explanation:
GNP का पूरा नाम सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (Gross National Product) है। यह एक देश के नागरिकों द्वारा एक निश्चित समय अवधि (आमतौर पर एक वर्ष) में उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल बाजार मूल्य है, चाहे वह उत्पादन देश के अंदर या बाहर किया गया हो। GNP में GDP (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) के साथ-साथ विदेशों से प्राप्त शुद्ध आय (Net Income from Abroad) को भी शामिल किया जाता है। यह एक महत्वपूर्ण आर्थिक संकेतक है जो किसी देश की आर्थिक सेहत को मापने में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:
GNP की गणना करते समय निम्नलिखित बातों का ध्यान रखना चाहिए:
1. इसमें केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को ही शामिल किया जाता है, मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं को नहीं।
2. GNP में हस्तांतरण भुगतान (जैसे पेंशन, बेरोजगारी भत्ता) को शामिल नहीं किया जाता।
3. GNP को कारक लागत या बाजार मूल्य पर मापा जा सकता है।
4. GNP में घिसावट (Depreciation) को शामिल किया जाता है, जबकि NNP (Net National Product) में इसे घटा दिया जाता है।

Explanation:

National Income Accounting is crucial for international comparisons and evaluating economic growth trends.

question:
If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero
Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply

Explanation:
The equilibrium point is where ex ante aggregate demand (AD) equals ex ante aggregate supply (AS). At this point, there is neither excess demand nor excess supply in the economy. This represents macroeconomic equilibrium, where total demand and total supply are balanced. If AD > AS, there will be excess demand, leading to rising prices, and if AD < AS, there will be excess supply, causing prices to fall. Thus, equilibrium is only possible when AD = AS.

Extra Facts:
Ex ante aggregate demand (AD) and ex ante aggregate supply (AS) are analyzed in the Keynesian model. AD includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports, while AS represents the total quantity of goods and services produced in the economy. The equilibrium income level occurs where AD = AS, bringing stability to the economy.

☛ What happens if AD > AS? → Price rise
☛ What is included in AD in the Keynesian model? → C + I + G + (X - M)
☛ When does equilibrium income level occur? → When AD = AS
☛ What happens when AS is higher? → Price fall

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: जहां प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग प्रत्याशित समग्र पूर्ति के बराबर है

जहां प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग प्रत्याशित समग्र पूर्ति से अधिक है
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जहां प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग प्रत्याशित समग्र पूर्ति के बराबर है

Explanation:
संतुलन बिंदु वह बिंदु होता है जहां प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग (AD) और प्रत्याशित समग्र पूर्ति (AS) एक-दूसरे के बराबर होते हैं। इस बिंदु पर, अर्थव्यवस्था में न तो अधिक मांग होती है और न ही अधिक पूर्ति। यह मैक्रोइकॉनॉमिक संतुलन का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है, जहां कुल मांग और कुल पूर्ति के बीच कोई असंतुलन नहीं होता। यदि AD > AS हो, तो मांग अधिक होगी, जिससे कीमतें बढ़ेंगी, और यदि AD < AS हो, तो पूर्ति अधिक होगी, जिससे कीमतें घटेंगी। इस प्रकार, संतुलन केवल AD = AS पर ही संभव है।

Extra Facts:
प्रत्याशित समग्र मांग (AD) और प्रत्याशित समग्र पूर्ति (AS) का विश्लेषण कीनेसियन मॉडल में किया जाता है। AD में उपभोग, निवेश, सरकारी खर्च और शुद्ध निर्यात शामिल होते हैं, जबकि AS अर्थव्यवस्था द्वारा उत्पादित वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की कुल मात्रा को दर्शाता है। संतुलन आय स्तर वह होता है जहां AD = AS होता है, और यह अर्थव्यवस्था में स्थिरता लाता है।

question:
In 1876, who prepared the first estimate of the national income of India?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Dadabhai Naoroji
PC Mahalanobis
VKRV Rao
William Digby
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji prepared the first estimate of India's national income in 1876. He detailed this in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'. His estimate suggested that India's per capita income was merely ₹20 per year, highlighting the economic exploitation under British rule. This study was a landmark in India's economic analysis and exposed the drain of wealth caused by colonial policies.

Extra Facts:
National income represents the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country in a year. Later, VKRV Rao (1931) and PC Mahalanobis (1950) also contributed to estimating India's national income. Mahalanobis played a key role in economic planning for India's Planning Commission.

question:
Which of the following terms define the Real National Income?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: GDP at current amount
GDP at constant price
GDP at average price
GDP at factors price
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GDP at constant price

Explanation:
Real National Income refers to the value of goods and services produced in an economy, measured at constant prices (base year prices). It eliminates the effects of inflation or deflation, reflecting the true growth of the economy. Measuring GDP at constant prices helps in accurately assessing changes in real output, rather than just price changes. It is a crucial tool in economics for analyzing economic growth and living standards.

Extra Facts:
Understanding the difference between Real GDP and Nominal GDP is essential. Nominal GDP is measured at current prices, while Real GDP is measured at constant prices. The GDP deflator is used to convert Nominal GDP into Real GDP. It helps separate changes in the price level from changes in output in the economy.

solution:

Explanation:

question:
Which of the following does not qualify as a source of factor income?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Profit
Donation
Wages
Rent
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Donation

Explanation:
Factor income refers to income earned by the factors of production (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship). Profit (for entrepreneurship), Wages (for labor), and Rent (for land) qualify as factor income. However, Donation is a voluntary transfer and not earned in exchange for any factor of production, hence it is not considered factor income. It is excluded from national income calculations.

Extra Facts:
Factor income is a key component in calculating national income metrics like GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and GNP (Gross National Product). Profit, interest, rent, and wages are all types of factor income. Transfers like donations, gifts, or government subsidies are not included in factor income because they are not earned through productive activities. Transfer payments do not contribute to current production.

[RRC GROUP D]

question:
Which of the following assumptions is made to determine the level of aggregate demand for final goods in the economy?
I. A constant final goods price and constant rate of interest over short run are assumed.
II. The aggregate supply is assumed to be perfectly elastic.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Only II
Only I
Neither I nor II
Both I and II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both I and II

Explanation:
In macroeconomics, two key assumptions are made to determine the Aggregate Demand (AD) for final goods in the economy. The first assumption is that the price of final goods and the interest rate are assumed to be constant in the short run, which helps in understanding the AD curve. The second assumption is that Aggregate Supply (AS) is perfectly elastic, meaning resources are unlimited in the economy, and the price level is not variable. Both these assumptions are crucial in the AD-AS model analysis and help in understanding short-term economic conditions.

Extra Facts:
The equilibrium between Aggregate Demand (AD) and Aggregate Supply (AS) determines the equilibrium income and price level in the economy. The AD curve depends on investment, government spending, exports, and consumption, while the AS curve is influenced by production costs and technological progress. Perfectly elastic AS implies the economy is in a recession with high unemployment, allowing resources to be available for increasing production. This is a key principle of Keynesian economics.

☛ What is the shape of the long-run Aggregate Supply curve? → Vertical
☛ What does equilibrium in the AD-AS model indicate? → Equilibrium income and price level
☛ Under what condition is AS perfectly elastic? → Recession
☛ What is the effect of an increase in AD? → Rise in income and employment
question_hi:
अर्थव्यवस्था में अंतिम वस्तुओं के लिए समस्त मांग के स्तर को निर्धारित करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी धारणा बनाई गई है?
I. अल्पकाल में नियत अंतिम वस्तु कीमत और नियत ब्याज की दर को मान लेते हैं।
॥. समस्त पूर्ति पूर्णतः लोचदार माना जाता है।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: केवल ॥
केवल I
न तो I और न ही ॥
। और ।I दोनों
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है । और ।I दोनों

Explanation:
समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र में, अंतिम वस्तुओं की समस्त मांग (Aggregate Demand - AD) को निर्धारित करने के लिए दो प्रमुख धारणाएँ बनाई जाती हैं। पहली धारणा यह है कि अल्पकाल में अंतिम वस्तुओं की कीमत और ब्याज दर नियत (constant) मानी जाती है, जिससे AD वक्र को समझने में सहायता मिलती है। दूसरी धारणा यह है कि समस्त पूर्ति (Aggregate Supply - AS) पूर्णतः लोचदार (perfectly elastic) होती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि अर्थव्यवस्था में संसाधनों की उपलब्धता असीमित है और कीमत स्तर परिवर्तनशील नहीं है। ये दोनों धारणाएँ AD-AS मॉडल के विश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण हैं और अल्पकालीन आर्थिक स्थितियों को समझने में मदद करती हैं।

Extra Facts:
समस्त मांग (AD) और समस्त पूर्ति (AS) के बीच संतुलन अर्थव्यवस्था में संतुलन आय और कीमत स्तर को निर्धारित करता है। AD वक्र निवेश, सरकारी खर्च, निर्यात और उपभोग पर निर्भर करता है, जबकि AS वक्र उत्पादन लागत और तकनीकी प्रगति से प्रभावित होता है। पूर्णतः लोचदार AS का अर्थ है कि अर्थव्यवस्था मंदी की स्थिति में है और बेरोजगारी अधिक है, जिससे उत्पादन बढ़ाने के लिए संसाधन उपलब्ध हैं। यह केनेसियन अर्थशास्त्र का एक प्रमुख सिद्धांत है।
